transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-05
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions), Marcus (Astrid CTO), Anika (Astrid ML Lead), Sanjay (Astrid Infra), Rita (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Astrid is building a chat+rerank experience for support agents. They want to understand unit economics and whether to start hosted then move to private. Budget band around $30-50k/mo. Concerns: data residency, KMS, latency under 300ms for live chat, pilot to validate cost/latency.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, quick intros. i'm jordan, AE at redwood.
00:12 Marcus: hey i'm marcus, cto at astrid, hi.
00:15 Anika: anika, lead on ML, i'll be owning model side.
00:18 Sanjay: sanjay infra, security/questions.
00:22 Jordan: cool, quick agenda: run through current stack and qps, target latency and cost goals, and then we can talk hosting options and pilot next steps. sound good?
00:30 Marcus: yep sounds good. our use case: customer support assistant that suggests answers and a reranker step we run over 10 candidates. about 200 agents, expectation of 6k user messages/day initially, spiky - mornings and eod.
00:48 Jordan: ok so 6k messages/day roughly, with rerank over 10 candidates means tokens multiply, what are your typical prompt lengths?
00:55 Anika: average prompt is about 250 tokens including context, reply target 60 tokens. reranker prompts are longer because we include full candidates, call that 800 tokens per rerank call.
01:10 Priya: so rough math, chat generate calls ~310 tokens, rerank ~800 tokens, multiply by volume - are you mostly agent-initiated or customer?
01:22 Marcus: mostly agent with some customer initiations. peak qps about 12-15 qps for short bursts, sustained maybe 3-4 qps.
01:30 Jordan: got it. what's your current hosting constraints? any need for private VPC or on-prem initially?
01:36 Sanjay: we need VPC and KMS integration for PCI-ish data. also audit logs are required for compliance. SOC2 is in progress. we prefer private deployment but open to starting hosted for rapid iteration if data flow can be tightly controlled.
01:50 Jordan: makes sense. Two common paths: hosted to get started, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and lower unit cost, or private (VPC/on-prem) for max isolation. we recommend a pilot to measure effective per-token burn with your prompt set and caching.
02:05 Marcus: can you share ballpark per-token pricing? we looked at other vendors and saw big differences.
02:12 Jordan: yes, for hosted our catalog models vary. ballpark: running a 70B-class open model on hosted may cost X cents per 1k tokens; dedicated quantized instances drop unit cost significantly. (note: redwood rep paraphrases numbers) importantly, batching and KV cache hit rate change the effective per-token cost by 20-60% depending on access patterns.
02:40 Priya: to put numbers concretely, if S=average sequence length and H=cache hit rate, effective tokens saved per request ~ H * cached_prefix_length. for rerank-heavy workloads your costs skew up because of the 800-token rerank calls.
02:55 Anika: we're worried about tail latency for agents. they need sub-300ms for the suggestion to feel instant. what are your latency SLOs on hosted vs dedicated?
03:05 Jordan: hosted can meet sub-300ms in many regions for smaller models and aggressive caching; for worst-case cold KV misses you may see 400-700ms. dedicated with reserved pools reduces variance and gives lower median / p95. private on VPC comparable if we colocate close to your infra, but initial setup and load profiling is needed.
03:28 Sanjay: what about quantization? would lower-precision models impact quality for our reranker?
03:34 Priya: yes, quantization (8-bit/4-bit) generally reduces cost and can speed up inference. rerankers sometimes are more sensitive; we usually run evaluation (ROUGE/accuracy) on a held-out set to measure degradation. Oftentimes 4-bit works fine for generation and 8-bit is conservative for rerank to keep accuracy. this is exactly what we'd test in a pilot.
03:58 Rita: any additional fixed costs with private? infra or software licensing?
04:02 Jordan: private has a platform fee and optionally an on-prem package. Dedicated has reserved monthly commits. We'll include both lines in the pricing sheet.
04:10 Marcus: do you support KMS/HSM for key management?
04:13 Jordan: yes, KMS integration and customer-managed keys available for private; hosted supports envelope encryption and customer key options for enterprise tiers. we'll include SOC2 and audit log docs.
04:24 Marcus: great. about caching - we expect a lot of shared prefixes because agents reuse response snippets, any way to estimate hit rate?
04:32 Priya: we'd ask for a sample token distribution and session traces. if you have lots of repeated prompts or shared system prompts, KV/prefix caching hit rates can be very high - up to 60-70% for certain support workflows. even 30-40% helps unit economics.
04:48 Anika: how do batch sizes affect latency vs burn? we can't batch too long or agents wait.
04:53 Priya: continuous batching tries to pack small requests within micro-batches to amortize kernel cost without adding perceptible latency. typical policy: bucket by target latency and burst profile. we can tune batching windows to trade a few ms for 10-30% lower per-token cost. we'll show concrete curves in the pilot results.
05:15 Marcus: sounds promising. how long to run a pilot to get statistically meaningful burn rates?
05:20 Priya: usually 2 weeks with representative traffic, or 1 week if you synthetic-amplify traces. we want live tails to see caching interplay.
05:27 Jordan: timeline idea: we run a hosted pilot first to validate workload and token burn, then move to dedicated/private if economics and compliance tradeoffs favor it.
05:35 Sanjay: onboarding time for private? network, keys, audits?
05:38 Jordan: private VPC onboarding typically 3-6 weeks depending on approvals; on-prem longer. dedicated provisioning for reserved pools is faster, often 1-2 weeks once contract is signed.
05:50 Marcus: ok budget band - we budgeted $30-50k/mo initially. can you show us likely burn scenarios for 3 price points?
05:58 Priya: yes in the pilot we'll produce low/medium/high burn scenarios using your prompt set. we'll include cost sensitivity to cache hit-rate, quantization, and batching policy.
06:10 Anika: about reranker - is it cheaper to run rerank as a single multi-candidate pass or multiple single-candidate calls?
06:17 Priya: multi-candidate is usually more efficient, fewer repeated prefix tokens. but inference memory and sequence length grow with candidates, so there's a tradeoff; often we do 10 candidates in one pass when possible.
06:30 Rita: any concerns about model fallback if capacity is constrained?
06:35 Jordan: smart routing can fallback to a slightly smaller model or to cached responses. we can set policy thresholds and TTLs for cached suggestions. we'll help design fallback policies in the pilot.
06:48 Marcus: competitors - we also tried vendor X and Y; they had simpler pricing but higher latency and no VPC offering.
06:56 Jordan: yeah we hear that a lot, Redwood tries to balance observability and routing controls.
07:02 Sanjay: on audit logs, can we get token-level logging redacted? we need traces but not PII in logs.
07:09 Jordan: yes, we support configurable redaction filters, and audit logs can include token counts and hashes instead of raw content for compliance. we'll share the security pack.
07:22 Anika: for evaluation metrics, what will you measure in the pilot?
07:26 Priya: latency p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm cache, effective tokens per request, cost per effective response, quality deltas for quantized models on our rerank set, and failure/retry rates.
07:40 Marcus: what's required from our side to start?
07:42 Jordan: three things: 1) sample prompt/token distribution and traces, 2) confirmation of pilot QPS windows and security requirements, 3) sign pilot statement of work.
07:55 Marcus: we can share token CSV and an initial 7-day trace. timeline: we can be ready by week of Jul 20.
08:02 Jordan: perfect. next steps recap: jordan sends pricing, priya sends benchmark plan, customer shares traces. schedule pilot kickoff week of Jul 20.
08:14 Marcus: agreed. thanks all.

End of transcript.
